Arshad Khan And Another vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 19
January, 2023

Bench: Vivek Kumar Birla, Saurabh Srivastava
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Court No. - 43
Case :- Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. - 305 of 2023
Petitioner :- Arshad Khan And Another
Respondent :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others
Counsel for Petitioner :- Mohammad Yaseen,Sayed Ahmad

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.
Hon'ble Vivek Kumar Birla,J.
Hon'ble Saurabh Srivastava,J.
Heard Sri Shamsuddin Ahmad holding brief of Mohammad Yaseen, learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri Yogeshwar Rai, learned State Law Officer for the State respondents.

The relief sought in this petition is for quashing of the F.I.R. dated 13.08.21022, registered as Case Crime No. 154 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506, 376 IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act,
Police Station Jaitpura, District Varanasi.
Further prayer has been made not to arrest the petitioners in the aforesaid case.
Submission of the learned counsel for the petitioners is that the offence as alleged in the first information report has not been made out against the petitioner.
He further submitted that against some of the co-accused persons charge sheet as well as final report have already been submitted.

sentences.text: Learned State Law Officer for the State-respondents points out that the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. is against the petitioner, therefore, cognizable offence has been made out.

It is further submitted that admittedly, as reflected from para 19 and 20 of the writ petition, Non-Bailable Warrants were issued against the petitioners and even proceedings under Section 82 Cr.P.C. has also been initiated as they are absconding.
We find that admittedly against some of the accused persons chargesheet and final report have been submitted in the present case.
Further, the petitioners are absconding and are facing coercive measures.
In such view of the matter, the present petition is not maintainable as the chargehseet in part cannot be quashed and in the present case cognizable offfence has been made out.

Therefore, in view of the law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of State of Haryana and others vs. Bhajan Lal and others, 1992 Supp. (1) SCC 335 and M/s Neeharika Infrastructure Pvt.
Ltd. vs. State of Maharashtra, AIR 2021 SC 1918 and in Special Leave to Appeal (Crl.) No.3262/2021 (Leelavati Devi @ Leelawati & another vs. the State of Uttar Pradesh) decided on 07.10.2021, no case has been made out for interference with the impugned first information report.
Therefore, the writ petition is dismissed leaving it open for the petitioners to apply before the competent court for anticipatory bail/bail as permissible under law and in accordance with law.
